steps.body: Surface area is a flat question wearing a 3-D costume. Cut a box along its edges and lay it out: what you get is a net, a flat arrangement of the same faces. Adding up the net's areas is adding up the solid's surface, because they are the same cardboard either way.

steps.body: Fold and unfold until the total matches.

widget.prompt: Set the box's dimensions so the unfolded net's total area is 52 square units.
widget.successFeedback: 4 by 3 by 2: the faces come in matching pairs — two 12s, two 8s, two 6s — and 2(12 + 8 + 6) = 52.
widget.lowFeedback: Total still under 52 — enlarge a dimension and watch which two faces grow.
widget.highFeedback: Total past 52 — shrink a dimension; each one controls exactly four of the six faces.

predict.prompt: A closed box has six faces. How many different face areas can it have at most?

options.label: Three — they come in matching pairs

predict.reveal: Opposite faces of a box are identical rectangles, so six faces carry at most three distinct areas. That pairing is why every surface-area formula for a box starts by doubling: you compute three faces and the box supplies their twins.

steps.body: Build one face of that net on its own.

widget.prompt: Build the crate's largest face: the 4 by 3 rectangle.
widget.factorFeedback: That rectangle covers 12 square units, but the face this net needs measures 4 by 3 — build those exact sides.
widget.successFeedback: 12 square units — and the opposite face is identical, so this single rectangle already accounts for 24 of the net's 52.
widget.lowFeedback: Face still under 12 square units — grow a side.
widget.highFeedback: Face past 12 square units — pull a side back in.

explanationVariants: A rectangular prism's net has six rectangles — three matching pairs.
Two ends, two sides, a top and a bottom: six in all.

widget.prompt: How many rectangles appear in the net of a rectangular prism?

options.feedback: Yes — three matching pairs, which is why surface area doubles three products.
That counts only the walls and forgets the top and bottom.
12 is the number of edges, not faces.

steps.body: So the formula is bookkeeping, not magic: 2(lw + lh + wh). Each product is one face; each 2 is that face's opposite twin. If you ever forget it, unfold the box in your head and add the rectangles — the formula will reassemble itself.

explanationVariants: The three distinct faces are 5×3 = 15, 5×2 = 10 and 3×2 = 6, and 2(15 + 10 + 6) = 62.
Compute three faces, double the sum: that is the whole method.

widget.prompt: A 5 by 3 by 2 box: what is its surface area, in square units?

commonErrors.feedback: That is the volume, 5×3×2 — how much fits inside, not how much wraps around.
That adds the three distinct faces (15 + 10 + 6) but forgets their opposite twins. Double it.

widget.successFeedback: 62 square units — three faces computed, three twins supplied by the box.

steps.body: Which faces does one dimension touch?
explanationVariants: Height appears in the lh and wh faces — four of the six.
Changing the height leaves only the top and bottom untouched.

widget.prompt: If you increase only the height of a box, how many of its six faces change area?

options.feedback: Right — the four side walls grow; the top and bottom keep their l×w area.
Only two faces avoid changing — the top and bottom. The other four all involve the height.
The top and bottom are l by w, with no height in them at all.

explanationVariants: A cube has six identical faces of 4×4 = 16, so its surface area is 96.
hints: A cube's faces are all the same square — how many of them are there?
Find the area of one face first, from the edge length 4.
One face is 4×4 = 16, and there are six of them.

widget.prompt: A cube has edge 4. What is its surface area, in square units?

commonErrors.feedback: That is the volume, 4³. Surface area wraps the outside: six faces of 16.
That is one face. A cube has six of them.

widget.fallbackFeedback: One face is 4×4 = 16; six faces give 6×16 = 96.
widget.successFeedback: 96 — the cube is the case where all three of the box's distinct faces coincide.

takeaways: A net is the solid's surface laid flat; adding its areas gives surface area.
A box's six faces come in three matching pairs, hence 2(lw + lh + wh).
Surface area is measured in square units; volume is not the same question.
steps.teaser: Next: run that formula on real boxes — and keep it clearly apart from volume.
